title: What If Abdul El-Sayed Became President?
note: Owner 29 Oct 2026: 1-min test = the first minute of a 10-min video 'what would change if Abdul El-Sayed became US president'. SENSITIVE: every claim below is in `sources`; real people are never voiced or given words they did not say; quotes are verbatim and attributed; claims by opponents are labelled as claims and paired with the fact-check. Hypothetical framing: he is a 2026 U.S. Senate candidate (Michigan), not a presidential candidate. 30 Oct 2026 hook rebuild (STYLE_3D §15.3): prize/result first ($33 M + still won), question at 6 s, promise at 10 s, info cards only after 12 s; punch lines p5/p6 (§16.1).

beats.text: Thirty three million dollars got spent to stop one man from winning one election
and he still won it by less than one point.
So what would happen if Abdul El-Sayed became the president of the United States?
Look at that crowd. When this man walks into a room people scream his name and when I walk into a room the dog leaves.
I want to be like him so badly that I bought a suit and the suit asked for a refund.
Stick around because by the end of this you will know exactly who would fight the hardest to stop him.
He is a doctor whose dad came from Egypt and right now he is running for the Senate in Michigan but today we are making him president.
And he really could because he was born in Michigan and the Constitution only asks that you are born an American and at least thirty five.
Remember those thirty three million dollars? A super PAC linked to AIPAC spent it in his Senate primary to help somebody else.
It did not work.
So he beat thirty three million dollars and you would think the hard part is over. It is not.
Because the current president keeps calling him Mohammed and wrote that he goes back to the days of the Jihad.
And El-Sayed answered that Trump knows his name is Abdul because he says it every day.
Nobody says my name every day. I tried.
His opponent even claimed he pledged support to the Muslim Brotherhood and a fact check found no evidence at all.
And all of this happened before he even got near the White House. So let us skip ahead and make him president anyway.
Day one. He picks up the pen for his biggest plan which is Medicare for All.
The idea is that the government becomes everybody's basic health insurance and the doctor bill goes to Washington instead of to you.
But then somebody asks for the price.
When Bernie Sanders had a plan like this the Urban Institute said it would cost about thirty four trillion dollars over ten years.
And a fellow at that same institute said that today it could cost close to double.
I checked my wallet. Not enough.
So who pays? El-Sayed says the rich should pay and he hopes to avoid raising taxes on most families.
But a budget watchdog said middle class taxes would have to rise for a plan like this.
And the same watchdog said a lot of families could still pay less overall than they pay today in premiums and copays.
So he signs it. And nothing happens.
Because a president cannot pass a law alone. A bill needs the Senate and most big bills need sixty votes to get past a filibuster.
Sixty senators agreeing on something this big is about the hardest thing in Washington.
So he tries something smaller. Your rent.
He wants to ban big corporations from owning homes and ban the computer programs that big landlords use to set rents.
Even though corporate buyers own only about two percent of the single family market. One house on a street of fifty. Rude house though.
And here he finally finds friends on both sides because Congress already passed a bipartisan bill that stops investors with three hundred and fifty homes from buying more.
Finally a win. And that is exactly when the money shows up.
Remember those thirty three million dollars? Cute.
By October the money spent in his Senate race had passed two hundred and five million dollars and it was on pace to be the most expensive election Michigan has ever seen.
Republican groups alone had spent fifty nine million dollars.
And the same AIPAC super PAC from the primary is reported to be sending up to nine million more to a group that backs his opponent Mike Rogers.
Have a guess how much the groups backing him had spent. Twenty three million.
He does have friends with money because Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez donated a million dollars to him.
I also donated. My coin is in there somewhere.
And keep an eye on Fox News because one of their hosts says something about him later that nobody expected.
But the money is not the worst part.
On October twenty fifth the current president held a rally in Port Huron Michigan.
And he told the crowd I'm here to keep a jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senator.
El-Sayed has said again and again that he is loyal to the United States and he has disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood.
When Mike Rogers questioned his loyalty in a debate El-Sayed called it shameful and said I'm proud of our Constitution that guarantees all of us the right to pray as we choose to pray.
And before that rally he even told the president Donald if you're watching don't wuss out man.
That is a real quote. I could never.
Even the interviews get rough because he once said being interviewed on CNN felt like and I am quoting him a non-consensual colonoscopy.
He is a doctor so he would know.
So picture month two. The money is against him and the math is against him and half the news is against him.
And then something weird happens. After a long and heated interview on Fox News the host Jesse Watters said he actually likes him.
Even Fox.
So can this guy run anything? In 2015 Detroit had just come out of bankruptcy and he was put in charge of rebuilding its health department at thirty years old.
In his first year the department more than doubled in size.
After the Flint water crisis his team tested the water in every Detroit public school building which was ninety four buildings and found nineteen schools with too much lead or copper.
I cannot even test my fridge.
But to be fair his campaign said he removed the lead and a news site found the fixes were temporary so the honest version is that his team found the problem.
His department also gave more than five thousand pairs of free glasses to kids in Detroit schools.
And remember those books from the very start? They are real. He wrote Healing Politics and a whole guide to Medicare for All.
Two books. I have a library card. It expired.
But then in 2018 he ran for governor and he lost that primary to Gretchen Whitmer.
So now we finally have everything we need to answer the question from the very start.

So who would fight the hardest to stop him? Not one single person. It is the hundreds of millions of dollars and the sixty votes he needs in the Senate and a country where half the people would fight every plan he has.
So would he change everything? Absolutely ... nothing in the first month. Because a president is a pen and Congress is the paper.

And remember he is not even a senator yet. Republicans have not won a Senate race in Michigan for more than three decades and he is up against Mike Rogers. If El-Sayed wins he would be the first Muslim senator.
And it all starts on November third.
Which one of his plans would you keep and which one would you throw out? Tell me in the comments.
Money talks so make sure yours says something smart. See you next time.
